answers.falsifier: with flock absent (rc 127) logtrim cuts a 200-line log to 10 and the caller shell survives, where the unedited logger leaves 201 and kills the caller ; with flock timing out (rc 1) the caller shell survives and no line is cut, where the unedited logger exits the caller
answers.how: In logtrim replace `flock -x -w 5 9 || exit 0` with: run flock; on rc 127 (not installed) go on unlocked, on rc 1 (timeout) return 0 from the function, never exit. Red-first proof bin/proofs/test_logtrim_trims_without_flock.py shadows flock with a shell function returning 127 and 1: (1) with 127 the 200-line log is cut to 10 and the caller survives; (2) with 1 the caller survives and no line is cut.
answers.title: logtrim keeps its cut when flock(1) is absent or times out, so the bash logger trims on Windows and never exits its caller's shell
answers.traces_to: Law 3: the red was measured at 201 lines on Windows and both teeth ran red on the unedited file; Law 7: a diagnostic surface may fail but must never take down the script it observes (the logger's own charter).
answers.what: bin/logger_for_bash logtrim trims when flock is not installed, skips the cut on a flock timeout without ending the caller's shell, and still serialises trims where flock exists.
